reasoning: Other: benchmarking / test-automation tooling (CLI). llm-d-benchmark is a Python CLI (`llmdbenchmark`, entry point llmdbenchmark.cli:cli) for benchmarking LLM inference on the llm-d stack. It handles the whole benchmark lifecycle: standing up llm-d deployments (standalone, modelservice, kustomize), running experiments through swappable load-generator harnesses (inference-perf, guidellm, vllm-benchmark), Design-of-Experiments parameter sweeps, smoketests, result collection/analysis and teardown. It is not an operator: there are no CRDs, controllers or reconcile loops. It is not a long-running service: the build/Dockerfile packages a toolbox image (oc, kubectl, gcloud, aws CLIs, harness scripts) for running benchmark jobs, not a server. pyproject.toml calls it a library, but its main purpose is a client-side CLI and harness images rather than a reusable dependency for other components. It does ship a lot of scenario/experiment YAML and templates (config/, experiments/), but that config feeds the tool and is not standalone platform configuration. The closest fit is a benchmarking/performance-testing CLI tool.
